whyItMatters: document.write() parses a string as live HTML at runtime. Any attacker-influenced fragment becomes cross-site scripting, and even static uses block parsing and violate strict Content-Security-Policy.
actions: Build DOM with document.createElement and textContent instead of HTML strings.
If HTML strings are unavoidable, pass them through an allowlist-based sanitizer first.
Re-run a SAST scan after the fix and confirm DPK-SAST-009 is no longer observed.
verification: The finding disappears on rescan and no document.write( call remains in the changed files.
